The liberation door of the Kinnara King Most Victorious Light Adornment (up to) "the karma from which he was born":
Great wisdom is universal compassion; these two are the fruits of adornment, the cause of all-knowledge, and the karma that can give rise [to them].
The Kinnara King Subtle Flower Banner attained the liberation door of understanding the retribution born of karma—
how karma is subtle and difficult to exhaust, yet reveals itself through self-observation to others.
The Kinnara King Power to Shake the Earth attained the liberation door of constantly initiating all manner of deeds that benefit sentient beings.
With supernormal powers he benefits sentient beings; his activity is uninterrupted and constant.
As the majestic lord of the Kinnara kings, he possesses the gate of liberation of skillful mastery and governance.

He knows the capacities of beings and transforms them through skillful means—namely, by gathering the mind through right wisdom and governing the mind as one would an object. 2. Verses in Praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the Kinnara King Sunlight of Good Wisdom (up to: spoke these verses:
"Whatever matters of peace and happiness exist in the world (up to: this fierce Lord is able to perceive them."
The sequence of the ten verses and their respective texts can be understood accordingly. △ Seventh, the Garuḍa King.

According to Xianshou’s *Jìngfǎ* (Mirror of the Dharma), it is stated that, based on the verses, the prose section omits the fifth king, Zhíchí (Upadhāraṇa). First, regarding the attainment of the Dharma in the prose:
Furthermore, from the Garuḍa King Mahāvegabala [up to] the liberation gate of universally observing the realm of sentient beings:
because his wisdom is unattached, he sees without obstruction; because it is not merely a partial observation, he thoroughly pacifies all.
From the *Abhirati-ratna-śikhara-garuḍa-rāja* (up to) the gate of liberation for teaching and transforming sentient beings:
they sit everywhere beneath the tree of enlightenment; this is called "abiding in the dharma-realm. Manifesting supernatural powers and preaching the Dharma is called "teaching and transforming."
The liberation door of the Pure and Swift Garuḍa King, [extending] to the power of diligence that accomplishes the perfections:
by exerting oneself in the various perfections and practicing them in the past, they are brought to fulfillment.
The Garuḍa King Adorned with the Non-Retrogressive Mind (up to) the Gate of Liberation Entering the Realm of the Tathāgata.

As for the realm, it is as stated in the verse: one enters through the transcendence of thought; only then is one truly courageous. Since the five versions were all missing this, I encountered a single version that contained it, which reads:
"The Garuḍa King who possesses the power to sustain and hold [beings] within the great ocean attains the ability to exhaust the suffering of sentient beings."

The "Gate of Liberation from the Ocean of Afflictions" is mostly missing from ancient manuscripts; we now rely on extant versions. However, these verses concern the ability to exhaust [the ocean], describing the Buddha’s merit and wisdom.
From the "Garuda King Firm Dharma Pure Light" up to the "Gate of Liberation through Discriminative Wisdom."
Because sentient beings are infinite, one achieves great wisdom.
This is like the Garuḍa King Crowned with a Diadem attaining the liberation door of adorning the city of the Buddha-dharma.
This city has three meanings: first, it defends against external enemies; second, it sustains the populace; and third, it opens its gates to attract and guide others. Now, it is said:
The City of Dharma encompasses the principles, teachings, practices, and fruits [of the path]. When practice accords with principle and teaching, then all aspects are simultaneously adorned;

thus, each possesses three meanings. That is to say: by realizing that the nature of the city of the mind is empty, the various delusions cannot enter; and by beholding the nature-endowed virtues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Thus, the myriad practices increase, and there is no path that is not traversed. Through the gathering and guidance of both self and others, one is able to accord with the fruit.
By severing the hundred negations, one achieves liberation; by nurturing all virtues, one perfects the Dharmakāya; and by opening up Prajñā, there is nothing that is not penetrated.
Only then is it revealed that within the city of the teachings, everything serves as a locus for nourishing the intended meaning. Every sentence penetrates the divine, and such abundance exists.
Because of its meaning, the verse says it is "vast and unfathomable. Since it possesses four gates in successive layers, it is without measure or number.
That which can ultimately elucidate this is none other than our World-Honored One.
The Garuḍa King Universal Swift Manifestation attained the liberation door of the indestructible power of equality.
Because the Dharma-body is signless, it is indestructible; its essence is suchness, wherein ordinary beings and sages are equal.
The dwelling in and realization of non-conceptual wisdom is called the power of accomplishment.
The liberation door of the Garuḍa King Samantadarśanasāgara (up to) manifesting forms for the sake of others;
manifesting forms identical to those of his own kind to skillfully subdue them.
The liberation door of the Garuḍa King Nāgarutasumegha (up to) passing away and being born with the practice of wisdom.
Sentient beings sink into and emerge from birth solely due to their karma and actions; only the Buddha’s wisdom regarding birth and death can universally penetrate them. 2.
Verses in Praise of the Buddha:
At that time, the Great Swift Power Garuḍa (and so forth) spoke these verses:
"The Buddha-eye is vast and without limit" (up to) "the liberation of the Dragon-Sound can be thus.
The verses and their explanations may be understood by correlating them in sequence. However, as for the fifth verse, there are some instances where it has been displaced;

therefore, I shall explain it briefly. The first two lines refer to its profound vastness; the next line refers to the mutual adornment of merit and wisdom. This practice extends through both cause and fruit. As for the cause...
The profound fruit is far-reaching and already inconceivable. Furthermore, there is one practice, which is the practice of the Tathāgata; that is to say, the Mahāyāna Mahāparinirvāṇa.
Thus, practice constitutes the fruit, and these fruits are all beyond the path of words—the practice of the Buddha, as described in the "Chapter on Manifestation."
△ Second, the eight asura kings. First, the prose section on their attainment of the Dharma.
Furthermore, Rāhu Asura King attained the liberation door of manifesting as the sovereign lord of excellence for the great assembly.

The Asura lords and others surpassed Mount Sumeru in height; yet the majestic radiance of the Tathāgata eclipsed the great assemblies of the ten directions, such that each being perceived him as their own supreme sovereign.
The Asura King Vemacitrin attained the liberation door of manifesting immeasurable eons.
He is able to perform various deeds with a single thread, causing many eons to appear within a single instant for the sake of training sentient beings and other such matters.
The Āsura King Skillful Illusionist (up to) the Gate of Purifying and Liberating the Suffering of All Sentient Beings.
By means of many dharma-gates, one enters the realm of the Buddha; thus, suffering is extinguished and the mind is purified. These various dharma-gates are also like illusions.
As the text below states: "Śambara" is the Sanskrit term for "skillful illusion."
The Asura King Mahāparivāra attained the liberation gate of self-adornment through the cultivation of all ascetic practices.
Through many eons and much suffering, he acted for the sake of others rather than himself—such as when Śibi rescued the pigeon or when the Sattva threw himself off a cliff.

These acts are already the most supreme adornment of a man of integrity; how much more so when one ultimately achieves tranquil wisdom and adorns oneself with the ten thousand virtues? By contrast, [worldly pursuits] reveal themselves to be of no benefit.
To undergo such toil and hardship is truly shameful. Because he acts for the sake of sentient beings, he possesses a great retinue.
The Asura King Bāhi has attained the liberation door of shaking the boundless realms of the ten directions.
By means of the power of great illusion, he moves the lands and awakens sentient beings according to their capacities; yet he does not terrify them—this is what constitutes "Great Power.
"Mahābala" (Great Power) and "Pāñcika" are merely different transliterations of the same term in Chinese and Sanskrit respectively.
The Asura King Samantaprabha attained the liberation door of establishing all sentient beings through various skillful means.
He opened various provisional gates to settle sentient beings in the bliss of the ultimate extreme; these provisional means serve as the foundation for entering the Great [Vehicle].
Therefore, all are causes for Buddha-wisdom; being undeluded regarding the provisional and the real constitutes universal illumination.
Firmly practicing the adornment like that of the Asura King [Vemacitra], they attain the liberation door of purifying all defiled attachments.
The myriad virtues accord with principle and are universally indestructible; this is the state of liberation wherein what defilement could fail to vanish?
Since all merit returns to Perfect Enlightenment, the verse says: "The power of the Buddha is such that those who cultivate it become firm, sublime, and majestic."
The asura king Vast Cause Wisdom attained the liberation door of "Lord of Non-doubt through the Power of Great Compassion.
It is not by the use of mere intellectual knowledge that he causes all to be free from doubt; it is because he who presides over this matter is Vast Cause Wisdom.
The liberation door of the Asura King Manifesting Supreme Virtue (extending to) serving and making offerings while cultivating various roots of goodness:
because there is supreme virtue in serving and cultivating goodness.
The Asura King Supraśabdita attained the liberation door of the practice of universal entry into all realms of existence with definitive equality.

He universally enters all destinies, and there is no field of knowledge (*vidyāsthāna*) to which he does not penetrate. A verse says: "Throughout the three periods of time, there is nothing that is not impartial;
possessing the Buddha-nature is called 'definitive. Endowed with these three meanings above, one practices with equality. To fail to proclaim the true meaning is not good.

This refers to sound. This preceding section, as well as the subsequent Night Goddess, both conclude by returning to the [proper] names; this pattern holds true for the preceding and following passages alike.
Fearing prolixity, I shall not explain them further. These two verses praise the Buddha in verse.
At that time, Rāhu, the Asura King, spoke these verses:
"All the vast assemblies throughout the ten directions... [praise] this King of Wondrous Sound."
The verses may be understood according to their sequence. △ Third, the various assemblies of deities. There are nineteen such assemblies. Now, first, the Lord of Daytime Deities (2).
First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, it was revealed that the Palace-Master Day-God attained the liberation door of universally entering all worlds.
With wisdom he understands the minds of beings, as space enters into form; his light illuminates the body and its environment, as the sun merges with the sky;
his body resides within the environment, like a reflection in a mirror. As the sovereign power of the world, he is able to encompass this body, and the nature of this body is equal to the world.
Because there is no interval [between them], they all enter by observing the capacities [of beings]; thus it is called "universal entry. The places where they enter become palaces.
This is the liberation door of the Daytime Spirit named Initiating the Fragrance of Wisdom, which leads [beings] to joy and satisfaction.
Because its meaning is perfect and accords with the capacities of beings, it fulfills the mind and accomplishes benefit.
This is the liberation door of the light of the Dharma called "Delightful" of the Day-Ruling Deity, Lord of Exquisite Adornments (up to).
The two lights of body and dharma are both delightful.
The Daytime Deity, Sovereign of Flower Fragrance and Wondrous Light, [attains] the liberation door of the mind of pure faith and understanding.
The rain of Dharma moistens the seeds; those already containing fruit are made to open, while those whose goodness has not yet sprouted are caused to awaken through faith.
The Daytime Spirit named Sovereign of Universally Gathering Wondrous Medicines attained the liberation door of the power of universally radiant light through accumulated adornment.
There is no dharma he does not awaken to; it is called the Power of Universal Radiance. Having cultivated and gathered [merit] throughout vast eons, he has perfected the adornment of wisdom.
The Day-God Joyful in Action, Master of the Eye of Joy (up to: ...), causes all to attain the liberation door of the joy of the Dharma.

Through skillful means, he reveals that worldly pleasure is also suffering, leading them to realization and entry [into the truth]. Their vision of the joy of the principle of the Dharma is like that of the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*).
The Lord of the Day, who universally manifests by observing the directions, attains the liberation door of the differentiated bodies of the Dharma-realm of the ten directions.

As for the clouds of the Tathāgata’s body: from the perspective of their essence, they are neither existent nor non-existent; yet, in relation to the capacities of sentient beings, they appear individually and pervasively throughout the ten directions, such that they cannot be said to be non-existent.
From the perspective of the Buddha, they accord with the true Dharma-realm, such that they cannot be said to be existent. This is, accordingly—
The dharmakāya, which is not a [substantially] existent phenomenon, constantly manifests without being distinct from phenomena;

by transforming through quiescent extinction, sentient beings—who are not non-existent—constantly establish themselves without being distinct from the Truth. This is precisely the differentiation within non-differentiation.
The Day-Walking Deity, Sovereign of Great Compassionate Power, attained the liberation gate of protecting all sentient beings and causing them to dwell in peace and attain deliverance.
Those in peril, he protects and brings to safety; those in distress, he rescues and brings to joy.
The Day-Ruling Spirit Light-Illuminating Root of Goodness attained the liberation door of the power of merit that universally generates contentment.

Sentient beings are shrouded in darkness by excessive desire and sink into the long night; [this spirit] awakens them through the Dharma, making contentment primary and endowed with the wisdom of contentment.
By the power of this merit, they are able to leave suffering behind and attain peace and happiness.
The Daytime Guardian Spirit named Wondrous Flower Garland (Supuṣpamālā), [extending] to the liberation gate through which all sentient beings who behold him obtain benefit.
Because he possesses awakened virtuous conduct, his fame is heard everywhere; since his merit is vast and his reputation high, his benefits are not in vain.
△ Second, verses in praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the Palace-Dwelling Day-Goddess manifested herself and spoke these verses:
"The Buddha’s wisdom is like space, without end; ... thus does one obtain the flower-garland of liberation."
The verse text may be understood as follows. △ Second, the Night Goddess [Rātridevatā] has two parts. First, the prose section on ten dharmas.

First, the night goddess is a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) of Sudhana regarding the tenth stage (*daśabhūmi*). Her realization and understanding are profound and vast, further manifesting the ocean-like assembly; her dharma-gate is inconceivable.

Furthermore, [the passage] from "the night goddess Samantaguṇaviśuddhaprabhā" to "the liberation door of great heroic valor" refers to Sudhana’s spiritual friend on the Stainless Ground (*vimalā-bhūmi*).
Her name is identical to that of the dharma-door, which is called "Universal Striding in the Joy of Tranquil Meditative Concentration.
The term "universal striding" (*samanta-vikrāmin*) refers to "great heroic valor. "Tranquil meditative concentration" (*śānta-dhyāna-samādhi*) refers to...
This concentration is the actualization of the Dharma and a dwelling in happiness; therefore, it is called "bliss. The "greatly courageous and valiant" refers to the function of concentration.
Being "valiant" means being capable, and being "courageous" means being fearless. This refers to seeing the pure faculties of the Buddha and sporting in supernormal powers (*abhijñā*);

hence, it is called "courageous and valiant," which is also synonymous with "striding forth. Because this courage and valor are vast and great, it is termed "Universal Virtue" (*Samantaguṇa*). It is the state where non-deluded wisdom and [the object] coexist.
This refers to the night goddess Viśvapadmasundarī (Pure Light), the Lord of the World who observes with eyes of joy, up to her gate of liberation characterized by pure and delightful qualities.
She is the spiritual friend of the stage of Prabhākari (The Radiant). Her name is Suvilokitajagat (Observing Sentient Beings with Joyful Eyes), and her liberation is named Mahāvega (Great Power).
"Powerful Universal Joy Banner" refers to this liberation. Because its virtues are complete without exception and its transformations are all-pervasive, it is called "Great Power.
Since it is currently vast and both body and afflictions are purified, there is no one who does not delight in seeing it; hence, it is called "Universal Joy.
Compassion constitutes its virtuous characteristic, which carries the meaning of a "banner. To observe this Universal Joy is termed the "Joyous Eye."
The night goddess *Lokapāla-tejo-mukha* attained the liberation door of universally manifesting in the world to discipline sentient beings;

she is the spiritual friend of the stage of *Arciṣmatī*. Her name is *Sarvasattva-trāṇa-suvimala-śrī*. "Guardian of the world's vital energy" (*lokapāla-tejo*) refers precisely to saving living beings;
because she protects life, the excellence of her virtues is revealed. The dharma gate is entirely the same, and the sequence is also...
One should consider that what is experienced must manifest before one, for the purpose of purifying it through cultivation.
Thus, the night goddess Samudrarutasvarā attained the liberation door of "Accumulating a Vast Heart of Joy."

This is the Good Friend of the Ground Difficult to Conquer (*Sudurjayā*). His name is Silent Ocean of Sound (*Śāntasvarasāgara*). The Dharma gate is named "The Adornment of Vast Great Joy Arising Moment by Moment.

"Arising moment by moment" has the meaning of accumulation, because one accumulates [merit] through seeing the Buddha and benefiting sentient beings. It gives rise to the adornment of great joy for two reasons:
first, seeing the Buddha cultivates the cause of joy, which adorns the fruit of delighting in seeing [the Buddha]; second, [benefiting sentient beings].
Accumulating this joy, her spirit was naturally adorned. From meditative concentration, she uttered a voice named "The Sound of Tranquility," as deep and vast as the ocean.
Thus did the Night Goddess Śrīsamudgatā attain the liberation door of profound, sovereign, and pleasing speech.
This refers to the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) of the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*). As for the phrase "protecting all cities and increasing power," the verse uses the term *śrī*.
In the Sanskrit language, this term contains two meanings: first, it means "auspiciousness" (*maṅgala*); second, it is translated as "to protect.

Therefore, it is later translated as *Bhadraśrī*, meaning "Worthy Head" (*Hsiian-shou*). Furthermore, because the phonetic value of the character "head" (*shou*) is the same [as *śrī*] while its meaning differs, it is rendered thus. Regarding that—
He acts as the leader. In the "Dharmadhātu" chapter, he serves as the protector; these are merely slight variations in the translator’s vernacular.
If one interprets them according to their meaning, the increase of power is itself the manifestation of universal auspiciousness, which corresponds precisely to the sequential dharma-gate.
Furthermore, it is identical to what is called the "liberation of profound, sovereign, and wondrous sound. Because it is a wondrous sound, it gladdens the mind; because it gladdens [the mind],...
Thus, with a purified mind, she is able to manifest from within stillness; therefore, she is named Sovereign.
The Night Goddess Who Causes Tree Blossoms to Bloom Universally has attained the liberation door of the treasury of vast joy and fulfillment of light.

This refers to the "Good Friend" of the Ground of Far-Reaching Travel (*dūraṃgamā-bhūmi*). Regarding the phrase "it causes all tree-flowers to bloom," it means that everything blooms, which is to say, they blossom universally.
This is a Dharma-gate. It is said that this refers to the "Bodhisattva’s Radiance of Vast Joy and Great Delight.
The phrasing is slightly inverted and abbreviated; the old translation states: "The Bodhisattva’s Radiance of Immeasurable Joy and Contentment. Here, "contentment" (*saṃtuṣṭi*) implies fulfillment.

The names are similar in their essence. This means that because he is able to know the Tathāgata’s skillful wisdom, which manifests the great merit, majesty, and radiance of the Dharma, he is called the Buddha Radiant Light (Prabhāsa).
Because he satisfies the minds of sentient beings with his merit and wisdom, he is named the One Who Contains Joy (Ratnākara).
The night goddess Samantabhadra-rakṣaṇī attained the liberation door of awakening sentient beings and causing their roots of goodness to mature;
she is a spiritual friend on the Immovable Bhūmi, known as Sarvasattva-paritrāṇa-mahāpraṇidhāna-vīryabalā.
The Dharma-gate called "Teaching and Transforming Sentient Beings to Cause the Arising of Roots of Goodness" and "Teaching and Awakening" differ in wording but are identical in meaning.

Both aim to cause [roots of goodness] to arise and reach maturity; they differ only in their starting points and endpoints. That is to say, manifesting supernatural powers and displaying signs are all for the purpose of taming and transforming;
causing all roots of goodness to grow and flourish, and protecting and nurturing them with equanimity, is precisely the great vow of diligent effort to rescue and protect all beings.
Therefore, she is able to do so; the current text is merely abbreviated.
The Night Goddess Joyful in Play has attained the liberation door of infinite compassion for protecting and rescuing sentient beings.
To cultivate this for a long time in every thought-moment and to constantly and exclusively provide rescue and protection is "boundless compassion" (*anantamaitrī*).

This is similar to the spiritual friend on the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) encountered by Sudhana, yet the phrasing differs considerably; furthermore, it does not follow that sequence. Therefore, I shall provide a direct explanation.
The Night-Spirit Always Joyful in All Faculties attained the liberation door of the gate of great compassion for universal manifestation and adornment.
Because she manifests an adorned body through the gate of great compassion for sentient beings who are difficult to transform due to the three poisons, she left her shadow in a stone cave;
even the poisonous dragon’s mental flowers were transformed, let alone when she manifested her physical form.
The Night Goddess Manifesting Pure Merit (up to) the Liberation Gate of Satisfying the Desires of All Sentient Beings.
Originally, for the sake of sentient beings, she perfected her own virtues so as to cause others' happiness to be fulfilled. △ Second, the verse praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the night goddess Samantāśubhavyūhaprabhā (up to) spoke these verses:
"You should contemplate the conduct of the Buddha (up to) stainless, dignified, and illuminating the ten directions."

The first phrase refers to the power of liberation being able to contemplate. The second phrase refers to the deity of tranquil bliss; because one contemplates the essence of the Buddha through this meditative concentration (*samādhi*), the subsequent sutra states:

"One universally beholds the Buddhas of the three periods of time without grasping or attachment," for one knows that the Tathāgata is signless (*animitta*) and that his nature and characteristics are fundamentally empty.
Therefore, it is called the "sign of tranquil emptiness. The following phrase refers to the Great...

"Valiant and courageous. According to the subsequent sutra, this refers to the simultaneous purification of both self and others. The next phrase refers to the fruit of meditative concentration (*samādhi*). The preceding section was explained in terms of the Buddha;

however, if explained in terms of the devas, then all four phrases are the functional application of meditative concentration. This is because by abiding in this liberation, one is able to perceive the essence, function, cause, and fruit of the Buddha.
All the worlds delight in seeing [him]... (up to) thus the World-Protector is able to observe.
Two or three [verses] may be understood [as follows]:
"In the past, the Buddha cultivated the ocean of joy... (up to) "this is what the one named Silent Sound understands."
The Universal Joy that accords with principle is vast and boundless; even though his inner mind remains unshaken, he manifests outwardly a majestic wrath that is all the more difficult to fathom.
The realm of the Tathāgata is immeasurable—[until] the goddess Samantakusumavikāsinī realized this path.

The preceding verse states that because it is quiescent, it is able to be pervasive; the subsequent verse states that because sentient beings are fundamentally pure from the beginning, this is quiescent extinction (*śānti*).

Thus, through wisdom, one exhausts the branches of delusion so that no principle remains unmanifest; through delusion, one penetrates to the source of the Real so that no confusion remains unexhausted.
Joy was fully satisfied.
[This concludes] the entry of the Great Spiritual Power Universally Manifesting in the Ten Directions (up to) the Spirit of Manifesting Blessings.
△ Third, the Principal Directional Spirits, in two parts. First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, the Universal Guardian Spirit of All Directions attained the liberation door of the power of universal protection;
he manifested his body and preached the Dharma, causing beings to awaken and attain the fruit—all through the power of protection.
From the Universal Manifestation of Radiance, Lord of the Directions, to the Gate of Liberation through the Supernatural Powers and Activities of All Sentient Beings:
the manifestation of signs through supernatural powers is the activity that brings about accomplishment; the emergence of sentient beings from suffering is the activity that is accomplished.
From the Light-Traveling Adornment Sovereign Directional Spirit up to the Great Radiance Liberation Door of Arising Joy and Bliss:
the light of the Dharma shatters darkness; when darkness is severed, wisdom arises. Wisdom arises together with the joy of the Dharma; with the severing [of darkness], one takes tranquility as bliss.
The presiding deity of the eastern direction attained the liberation door of "universally manifesting in all places without obstruction or vain effort.
By universally manifesting the preaching of the Dharma, delusions are necessarily extinguished upon hearing it; therefore, it is not in vain.
From "The Lord of the Direction Deity Who Permanently Severs Delusion" to "The Gate of Liberation that Generates Meritorious Qualities":
Sages have no names; names are established in accordance with things. What is valued lies solely in the generation of virtues and the extinction of delusions.

From "The Gate of Universal Roaming in the Pure Space, the Lord of the Quarter Deity" (up to) "The Gate of Causing Sentient Beings to Attain Joyful Liberation," items sixty-six and sixty-seven may be understood accordingly.
From "The Gate of the Lord of the Quarter Deity with Unconfused Topknot and Eyes" (up to) "The Gate of Undifferentiated Sovereign Power."

Karma and its common nature are both empty; yet their retributions are never lost, and there is no difference between them. Their nature and characteristics are unimpeded, functioning as a power of mastery.

To delude [beings] regarding their retribution, one speaks of it so that they may eliminate evil karma; to show that the nature of karma is empty, one speaks of it such that even wholesome karma perishes.
The Universal Contemplation of the Lord of the World, the Deity of the Four Directions (up to) the Gate of Liberation through Various Karmas within All States of Birth.

The preceding section explained the nature and characteristics of karma to cause beings to sever their karmic bonds; this section concerns the knowledge of the distinctions among karmas, so that one may transform others according to their individual capacities.
[He enters] the liberation door of universally visiting the presiding deities of the directions (up to) generating joy in all sentient beings.
Among worldly people, none lack a beginning, yet few are able to reach the end. Now, because the Sage possesses both aspiration and capability, his undertakings are brought to completion.
Worldly people follow their desires and cannot abandon both [extremes]; now, because he possesses both compassion and pity, [he is able to do so].

Causing sentient beings to rejoice refers to the ten pāramitās, all of which are brought to ultimate perfection, and the four immeasurable states of mind (*catur-apramāṇa*), which cause sentient beings to be filled with joy.
△ Second, the verses in praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the Universal Abiding Lord of the Directions (up to) spoke these verses:
"The Tathāgata’s sovereign gateway to appearing in the world... this is the liberation of the Universal Wandering Deity."
The sequence of the ten verses may be understood through their respective explanations. △ Fourth, the Lord of the Sky Devas (two parts). First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma:
Furthermore, the Lord of the Sky Devas, Pure Light Universally Illuminating... [up to] ...the gate of liberation of the minds of all sentient beings.
When wisdom constructs principle, the ten eyes shine far and wide; when the sun and moon merge with space, the myriad forms appear clearly.
The Sovereign Spirit of Profound and Vast Wandering attained the liberation door of universally entering the Dharma-realm.
The two lights of body and wisdom pervade the entire dharma-realm;
the Wind-Master of Auspiciousness, Lord of the Space Devas, attained the liberation door of the physical form that realizes the boundless realm.
The Buddha’s body is like space; it is a boundless realm, unarisen and unstained. It acts as the auspicious wind.
The Lord of the Space-dwelling Spirits, Free from Obstructions, attained the liberation door of being able to eliminate the obstacles of karma and delusion for all sentient beings, just as one.
Extensively explaining the noble path, one leaves behind the three obstacles and dwells securely in the two kinds of emptiness.
The Space-Ruling Spirit Wondrous Topknot of Broad Steps attained the liberation door of contemplating the ocean of vast practices through universal observation.
Seeking the supreme above and transforming those below is called the Vast Practice. To bring peace to sentient beings is like the exquisite crest-jewel.
This is the liberation door of the Space-Ruling Spirit Unobstructed Radiant Flame, who universally rescues and protects all sentient beings from calamities and brings them to liberation.
Sinking into the calamities and hardships of birth and death, they are rescued by the light of compassion and wisdom.
[This concludes the section on] the Sovereign Space Deity of Unobstructed Supreme Power, up to the Gate of Liberation through the Power of Merit Free from Attachment.
That merit and wisdom do not obstruct one another but mutually guide each other is called supreme power.
This is the liberation door of "Stainless Radiance," presided over by the Space-Ruling Spirit, which leads to the purification that is free from all hindrances.
Delusion is dispelled by wisdom.
The space-ruling spirit Master of Profound and Wondrous Sound attained the liberation door of the light of wisdom that universally perceives the ten directions.
Her wondrous voice speaks with excellence.
The World-Space Ruling Spirit, Pervasive Light Throughout the Ten Directions, attained the liberation door of manifesting throughout the world without leaving its original location.
Without departing from its original place, it resonates throughout the ten directions. II. Verses in Praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the space-ruling spirit Pure Light Shining Everywhere (up to) spoke these verses:
"The Tathāgata’s vast eyes are pure like space... seen by the auspicious wind."
The three emptinesses have four meanings, which encompass five dharmas: 1. To be free from the arising of the grasper (*grāhaka*) is to sever deluded conceptualization (*vikalpa*). 2.
To be free from the characteristics of the grasped (*grāhya*) means there is no characteristic and no name. 3. That objects lack intrinsic nature (*svabhāva*) is precisely suchness (*tathatā*).

4. That the mind has nothing to be attained is correct gnosis (*samyag-jñāna*). Delusion regarding suchness gives rise to names and forms; this is the arising of deluded conceptualization. Awakening...
The suchness that is the root of names and marks, when grasping is overturned, becomes wisdom. Outside of suchness there is no wisdom; the essence of wisdom is itself suchness.
These two are like space—tranquil illumination without obstruction. To see the Buddha in this way is the auspiciousness of this day.
The Tathāgata, throughout immeasurable kalpas, has extensively expounded all the noble paths that universally extinguish the obstacles of sentient beings.

While the prose section and the list both refer to this as "abiding securely" (an-zhu), here it is called "perfect radiance" (yuan-guang). Perfect radiance symbolizes wisdom (*prajñā*), while abiding securely symbolizes meditative concentration (*samādhi*).
These two factors support one another; whether mentioned earlier or later, both are capable of extinguishing obstacles, and there is no contradiction in principle.
I contemplate the bodhisattva practices accumulated by the Buddha in the past... [up to] "...the unimpeded divine power can see.

Regarding the "ocean of birth and death," the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* (Treatise on the Stages of Yoga Practice), fascicle 70, states: there are five characteristics that cause it to resemble birth and death and to receive the name "great ocean":
first, because its location is boundless; second, because it is profound; third, because it is difficult to cross; fourth, because it is... [text fragment].
Because it is drinkable; because it is the locus of the five great jewels. The commentary states: By means of the first four meanings, sentient beings transmigrate;
by means of the fifth meaning, Bodhisattvas enter it. To provide a partial illustration, the *Ninth Decade* (*Daśabhūmika*) states that for three reasons it is not the same as the ocean of water:
first, their intrinsic natures differ, in that the ocean of water is merely one part of the aggregate of form; second, [the difference in] drowning...
There is no difference in their submergence, as both humans and animals likewise sink and because they both sink with the body. Regarding the three types of crossing over, there is a difference:
those who have not yet abandoned desire are also able to cross over the ocean of birth and death; the opposite of this should be considered accordingly.
"The treasury of pure merit can serve as a field of blessings for the world" (up to) "universally manifesting and being able to observe.
The remaining four [phrases] may be understood accordingly. △ Fifth, the Wind-Ruling Spirits, in two parts: first, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.

Furthermore, from the wind spirit Unobstructed Radiance Lord down to those who have attained liberation through all worldly gates, they employ the wind of skillful means to unite with the sun of wisdom-light. Thus, their wisdom enters profound dharmas without obstruction;
their bodies enter the world yet remain without shadow.
The Bodhisattva Universal Manifestation of Heroic Sovereignty, Lord of Wind Spirits, [up to] the liberation door of making vast offerings whenever a Buddha appears.
The Bodhisattva, with the great mind seeking enlightenment, holds offering implements that accord with reality and are equal to space.
It is vast; it is not hindered by the multiplicity of phenomena. With a body that is the entirety of the dharma-realm, one makes offerings to infinite Buddhas in a single thought-moment.
Just like the power of the wind, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished.
From the wind spirit Cloud Banner Master (up to) the liberation door of universally extinguishing the illnesses of all sentient beings:
when a long wind suddenly arrives, floating clouds disperse and vanish; when the wind of compassion suddenly arises, the diseases of delusion and suffering perish.
The wind deity Sovereign of Pure Light Adornment (up to) the liberation door of causing the mountain of heavy obscurations to be crushed and destroyed.
By the wind of the adornment of merit and wisdom, the obstacles that are like mountains are demolished.
The power of the Wind Deity who can exhaust the waters is able to shatter the boundless hosts of Māra; this is the gate of liberation.
The Ten Powers subdue Māra and utterly destroy the ten armies. He alone is named "Exhauster of Waters" because sensual craving is the foremost [of the defilements].
The Wind Spirit named Great Roar Pervading Everywhere attained the liberation door of eternally extinguishing all fear in sentient beings.
With the compassionate voice from his pores, he eliminates the five fears; even if a hundred apertures were blown upon differently, his pervasive roar would delight all according to their capacities.
From the "Wind-Spirit Lord Whose Topknot Hangs from the Treetop" (up to) the "Liberation Gate of the Ocean of Eloquence Regarding the True Reality of All Dharmas.
Because wisdom enters into true reality, its wondrous eloquence is like an ocean; just as the wind strikes a tree, it is able to hang down.
The wind spirit Universal Conduct Unhindered Lord attained the liberation door of the treasury of skillful means for taming all sentient beings.
Because these skillful means for taming beings are that which wisdom enters, they are called a "treasury."
The various palace-dwelling wind spirits [attain] the liberation door of extinguishing the darkness of extremely heavy ignorance.

Because they move freely between both meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*) within the palace of dhyāna, they are able to extinguish the darkness of ignorance. From the perspective of the Buddha, movement and stillness are non-dual;
thus, upon seeing him, ignorance is necessarily extinguished.
From the Wind Spirit Great Light Shining Universally (up to) the liberation door of the power of unimpeded action for all sentient beings:
Just as the sun and moon shine and are not moved without the wind, so too is the power of skillful means in the unimpeded movement of wisdom.
△ Second, the verse praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the wind spirit Unobstructed Radiance (up to) spoke these verses:
"The Dharma of all Buddhas is profoundly deep... this is what the spirit Universal Illumination has seen."
(Entering the Fourth Sūtra). △ Sixth, the Fire-Ruling Deity. The prose section contains ten dharmas. Some say that according to the Sanskrit original, the fourth is missing here.
Furthermore, the Fire-Ruling Deity Samantārciṣmatigarbha attained the liberation door of "completely eliminating all darkness in the world."
By means of the power of progress, he manifests in the world to eliminate the ignorance regarding phenomena. Because it is the foremost, he specifically accords with the meaning of fire.
Thus, the Lord Fire God Radiant Banner (Prabhāketu) [leads sentient beings] to the gate of liberation from the suffering of drifting in various delusions and the heat of affliction.
Delusion has two meanings: first, drifting; second, affliction. Through skillful turning back, one can extinguish it.
The Fire God Great Light Pervasive Illumination attained the liberation door of the treasury of great compassion and the power of immovable merit.

The auspicious marks of merit that accord with the nature of reality are unmoved by delusion and united with great compassion; being unmoved in self-benefit, they are able to encompass all virtues and are called the inexhaustible treasury.
Some say that, according to the Sanskrit original, the name of the deity is *Jinajyotirviśvaprabha* (Victorious Supreme Flower-Light Universally Illuminating).

This dharma gate is named "Universally Able to Remove the Dust of Afflictions," meaning that because his practice has been perfected throughout oceans of kalpas, he is now able to manifest supernormal powers to extinguish delusions.
The verse says: "The Spirit of the Palace of Myriad Wonders. This shares the same name as listed previously. "Myriad Wonders" (Zhòngmiào) carries the sense of "supremely excellent";
however, most editions lack this term, though some editions state it in full as: "The Fire Spirit, Lord of the Palace of Myriad Wonders, attains..."
The liberation door of great compassion providing vast shade for all sentient beings—this may be a scribal omission.
The fire-governing spirit Endless Light Topknot attained the liberation door of illuminating the boundless realm of empty space with radiance.

Regarding the phrase "the radiance shines forth," it is like sunlight merging with space; as equal to space, it is boundless. Wisdom accords with the true reality (*dharmatā*); as corresponding to reality, it is limitless.

Although accomplished through cultivation over vast eons, it is entirely identical to what is primordially possessed. Exhausting the spirit and reaching the ultimate limit of calculation, its wondrous perfection is inconceivable.
It is truly the root of delusion, yet it is the direct cause (*hetu*). When wisdom illuminates the source of the mind, it is the revealing cause (*pariniṣpatti-hetu*). It is like space.
Regarding the sun: I shall now briefly set forth ten points to clarify its inconceivable nature. First, the sun and space are neither identical nor separate.
Second, it neither abides nor does it not abide. Third, the sun skillfully acts as a favorable condition for destroying darkness, which is essential for revealing space.
Fourth, although it destroys darkness and reveals space, space itself is neither benefited nor harmed. Fifth, in principle there is indeed no harm; yet in terms of phenomena, [it appears otherwise].
6. By extension, when darkness is forever removed, the nature [of space] does not increase; yet all myriad phenomena appear within that which contains the realm of emptiness.
Although the nature of this empty space is pure, if there were no sunlight, then darkness would arise.
7. It is not because the empty space is itself void that it can naturally remove darkness. If darkness is to be removed, it must depend upon the sunlight. 8. As for the sun...
9. There is no emptiness; there is no light and no illumination. If emptiness were without the sun, darkness would not be dispelled of its own accord.

Thus, the nature of this darkness neither comes nor goes, and the essence and characteristics of the sun likewise neither arise nor cease. 10. It is simply that when the sun shines upon the sky, heaven and earth become brilliantly clear.
When the sun of wisdom shines upon the emptiness of the mind-nature, there are likewise ten meanings; reflect upon them according to the analogy.
This does not merely explain this single passage; rather, it reaches far to encompass all the scriptures, synthesizing the preceding and following sections.
It concerns the liberation door of the fire-governing deity *Vicitrārciḥprabhāsaśāntavicitrābharaṇa*, who has attained various blessings and adornments.
The essence is quiescent yet gives rise to illumination; this is called the Light of Quiescence. By means of this, one accomplishes merit to adorn the physical marks.
In the palaces of the ten directions, the Fire-Governing Deity Sumeru-uttara (attains) the gate of liberation for awakening to all worlds.
The seventh and eighth [stages] may be understood accordingly.
The Fire-Controlling Spirit of the Ten Directions, Illuminating Radiance, attained the liberation door of "Permanently Destroying All Ignorant Attachment and Views.

By discerning the characteristics of phenomena (*dharmalakṣaṇa*), he was forever free from the ignorance of non-comprehension; by awakening to the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), he became free from attachment.
He saw the fire-god Vajrasphoṭavidyutprabha, who attained the liberation door of the great thunderous roar that accomplishes all powers of aspiration.
Because he supported his aspirations through practice, he was able to manifest in the world and let out a lion’s roar, praising the Buddha with two verses.
At that time, the Fire God named Universal Radiant Flame Treasury (up to) spoke these verses:
"Observe the power of the Tathāgata’s diligence" (up to) "this is what the spirit Vibration Sound understands."
The fourth verse is added; the rest may be understood as before. △ Seventh, the Water-Ruling Deity, in two parts: first, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, the Water-Ruling Deity named Universal Cloud Banner [attains] the gate of liberation of compassion that benefits all sentient beings.
Great compassion that is without conditions is called equality.
The water-ruling spirit Cloud-Sound-Tide obtained the liberation door of the adornment of boundless dharmas;
through these boundless practices, she adorns both herself and others.
The Water Spirit Wondrous Color Topknot attained the liberation door of universally gathering and transforming through skillful means according to those who should be converted.
Remaining tranquil and unmoving, he accords with and gathers beings by observing their capacities and responses;
thus, in winter the snow accumulates in pure white, and in summer there is nowhere water does not flow.
The Water-Ruling Spirit Skillful in Vortices attained the liberation door of universally expounding the profound realms of all Buddhas;
with wondrous voice, she expounds the deep intent of the Buddhas, causing others to awaken to the vortices of the sublime Dharma.
The water-ruling spirit Free from Defilement and Accumulated Fragrance attained the liberation door of the universal manifestation of great pure light;
the two lights of body and wisdom universally awaken and transform beings, filling the entire dharma-realm with purity and stainlessness.
The Water-Ruling Spirit Guangyin of Fugao attained the liberation door of the pure dharma-realm that is signless and devoid of intrinsic nature.
Having realized the pure dharma-realm where both nature and characteristics are utterly transcended, his virtues are nowhere unseen, and thus his great function never ceases.
The Water Deity Sovereign of Contentment attained the liberation door of the inexhaustible ocean of great compassion.
Because sentient beings are inexhaustible, great compassion is inexhaustible; it is full yet does not overflow, thus possessing the meaning of contentment.
Flowing or ceasing according to conditions—this is sovereignty.
From the Water-Ruling Spirit Pure Joy and Auspicious Sound (up to) the Liberation Gate of the Treasury of Great Joy:
because one sees the Buddha everywhere, great joy is inexhaustible. This joy arises from the Buddha; thus, the Buddha is called the "Treasury.
If one listens to the sound of flowing springs, there is nothing that does not bring delight.
From the Water-Spirit Sovereign Who Universally Manifests Majestic Radiance, up to the Universal Manifestation of Liberation through Vast Power of Merit:

because their merit is characterized by the non-obstruction of nature and appearance, they are able to universally manifest spiritual powers, like a stream where emptiness and form reflect one another.
His majestic radiance flows boundlessly;
his roar pervades the ocean. [This is] the liberation door of the Water-Ruling Deity’s skillful means for subduing through an inspiration as vast as space.
His conduct in taming sentient beings is as expansive as the void; its infinite function never pauses for a moment, inexhaustible like space. △ Second, the verses:
Praising the Buddha with verses:
At that time, the water spirit named Cloud Banner Universally Arising (up to: spoke these verses:
"The gates of pure compassion are as numerous as the atoms of the lands; [therefore, those who see them never tire of doing so]."

The first half [of the verse] distinguishes the cause and effect of the single mark; the next line illustrates the remainder; and the final line distinguishes the benefit. Regarding the initial term "pure":

it is because it is free from faults and lacks [conceptual] conditions. Regarding "the gates are as numerous as motes of dust": it is because they provide benefit and happiness according to what is appropriate.
Taking compassion as the cause, one attains the fruit of the wondrous marks; taking the marks as the cause, one attains the fruit of being never-weary. However, the Tathāgata’s marks are purely...

There is admixture. This is from the perspective of the "pure" gate (*śuddha-mukha*). If one considers it from the perspective of the "admixed" gate (*miśra-mukha*), then every single characteristic and every single hair-pore encompasses the entirety of the Tathāgata’s practice within the *dharmadhātu*.

This is true for every characteristic without exception. Thus, purity and admixture are non-obstructive; cause and effect are mutually integrated; and what is perfectly accomplished (*pariniṣpanna*) is not a partial accomplishment.
Therefore, a single characteristic and a single hair-pore of the Buddha are identical to the *dharmadhātu*, possessing no measurable limits. This is the spiritual power...
From a single gate of compassion, one enters into inexhaustible marks. This refers to the characteristics of the ten bodies (*daśakāya*).

As for the causes of the thirty-two marks, they are explained as being merely a single mark and a single cause, as found in treatises such as the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* and the *Yogācārabhūmi*, and in sūtras such as the *Nirvāṇa-sūtra* and the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*.
These shall be cited in the "Chapter on the Ocean of Marks" (*Lakṣaṇasamudra-parivarta*).
From "When the World-Honored One was practicing in the past" up to "the place frequented by the goddess Subhāvarta," the three preceding verses have clear wording and are easily understood.
From "The radiance of the World-Honored One is inexhaustible" up to "as observed by the goddess Viśuddhagandhā," [the meaning is as follows:]
The first phrase, "inexhaustible," reveals the permanence of the light. The next, "pervading the dharma-realm," distinguishes the omnipresence of the light.
"Inconceivable" reveals the profundity of the light; for it manifests form while not being form—it manifests blue and yellow without being blue or yellow.
This third phrase reveals the functional activity of the light.
The Tathāgata is pure and equal to space... [the sound of] his roar pervades the ocean; one who can enter this [is truly capable].
*Da fangguang fo huayan jing shu*, Scroll Nine.
*Da fangguang fo huayan jing shu*, Scroll Ten (entering the third sheet of the fourth scroll of the sutra).
Composed by the Śramaṇa Chengguan of Mount Qingliang;
recorded and annotated on the sūtra by the Śramaṇa Jingyuan of Jinshui. △ Section Eight:
The Principal Ocean Deity. Part One: The Long Prose Exposition on Ten Dharmas. (The third verse is omitted.)
Furthermore, from the ocean spirit named Manifesting Jewel Light (up to) the liberation door of a body adorned with various jewels:
by making offerings to the Buddhas for the sake of sentient beings, through the merit of such giving, one attains the marks of various jewels to adorn the body.
From the Ocean-Dwelling Spirit named Indestructible Vajra Banner Leader (up to) the Gate of Liberation for Protecting the Roots of Goodness of All Sentient Beings:
skillfully according with their faculties and desires, he teaches the Dharma to protect their goodness, causing it to grow and mature.
The Ocean-Ruling Deity Unmixed with Dust and Defilement attained the liberation door of being able to exhaust the ocean of afflictions of all sentient beings.
This means expounding the profound and vast Dharma, realizing that the essence of afflictions is empty. A verse in the Sanskrit original says:

"The great rain from the Dharma-clouds of the Teacher of all paths in the world is unfathomable; it dries up and exhausts the infinite oceans of suffering. This is the state free from dust and defilement."

Entering the Dharma-gate. Regarding "suffering" (*duḥkha*), according to this text, it means to exhaust the ocean of suffering. Fourth, if one perceives the realm of the Buddha, then delusion perishes and suffering ceases.

According to the extant scriptural text, the third refers to afflictions (*kleśa*) and the fourth refers to suffering. However, if one follows the Sanskrit original, suffering comes first and delusion follows.
Since the translators have omitted [the correct order], the text and its meaning have become inconsistent; thus, the ancient masters remarked that [the text] was corrupted by omission.
The fourth verse: Since the names [of the gates] are identical, it is known that one is liberated from the third.
The Ocean Deity, Lord of the Ever-Rolling Waves, attained the liberation gate of enabling all sentient beings to leave the evil realms behind.
The waves are ever-present; this is the universal application.
Taking water as his palace, the auspicious ocean deity Jewel Moon Lord attained the liberation door of universally extinguishing the great darkness of ignorance.
One extinguishes delusion through wisdom.
The ocean-dwelling spirit named Wondrous Flower Dragon Topknot attained the liberation door of extinguishing all suffering in the various realms of existence and bestowing peace and bliss.
"That which is subject to the transitions of conditioned activity is entirely suffering. When the cause of Bodhi arises, birth and death cease and suffering perishes; thus one attains [liberation]."

The ocean spirit Universal Sustainer of Radiant Flavor [attains] the liberation door of the nature of liberation from the delusions of all sentient beings' various views, which is the blissful tranquility of nirvāṇa.
Using wisdom to extinguish delusion does not yet free one from views; by thoroughly understanding the nature of both delusion and views, delusion and views vanish of their own accord.
To contemplate the true and the false as equal is the realm of the Buddha.
The Ocean-Ruling Spirit Jewel-Flame Flower-Light (up to): The Liberation Door of the Bodhicitta of the Spiritual Lineage. All sentient beings possess the Buddha-lineage;
it is perfectly luminous and precious, endowed with virtues and thus called a "jewel. The Buddha’s eye surveys all universally, and the Buddha’s wisdom reveals all universally.
The primary cause is now manifest, like the extraction of gold from its ore. If the Great Mind arises, it is like planting a seed.
Because sprouts arise, it is called "birth. The two causes—the conditional (*pratyaya*) and the perfecting (*pariniṣpanna*)—constitute the wondrous path for awakening.
The ocean-dwelling spirit Vajramakuṭādhipati attained the liberation door of the ocean of merit of the immovable mind.
When one realizes [reality] as it is and does not grasp at it, the mind remains unshaken, as tranquil as a still ocean, and all myriad virtues converge therein.
Thus, even if Mount Sumeru could be toppled, how could Māra possibly disturb such a state? To subdue Māra in a single thought is as described in the *Saṃyukta-avadāna*.
The oceanic deity Sovereign of the Sound of Thundering Tides attained the liberation door of the samādhi gate of universal entry into the dharma-realm.
Entering the concentration of the dharma-realm, he pervaded it as extensively as the dharma-realm itself. △ Second, the verses in praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the ocean-ruling spirit named Jewel Light Manifestation (up to) spoke these verses:
"The inconceivable ocean of great eons... [is] the sphere of activity of the spirit Ocean Tide Sound."
△ Second, the Nine Lords of River Deities. First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, the Lord of River Deities named Universally Emitting Swift Currents attained the liberation door of universally raining down boundless Dharma-rain.
The Practice of Forming Rain: If it pours down in great torrents, it extinguishes delusions and gives rise to virtue; like a swift-flowing river, it is free from all obstructions.
[This practice] universally purifies springs and streams, and for the River-Gods, it leads to the gate of liberation through eternal separation from afflictions.
Manifesting her form to pacify afflictions; if one washes the mind in her springs and streams, she purifies the eyes by removing worldly dust.
This is the liberation door of the River Goddess (to: who universally cleanses the defilements and impurities of the delusions of all sentient beings.
Truly washing away defilements, compassion and wisdom support one another like a deep, clear pool where emptiness and form reflect each other;
thus it is called the "Pure Eye Free from Dust.
The River Lord named Universal Roar Throughout the Ten Directions attained the liberation door of the "Eternal Sound of the Ghaṇṭā that Benefits Sentient Beings."

The perfect voice benefits all universally. Like crashing waves producing resonance, the River Goddess, Sovereign Who Universally Protects and Saves Sentient Beings, [attains] the liberation door of constantly giving rise to compassion that is free from affliction and harm.
"Saving those who are drowning:
the river goddess Anuṣṇāprabhāvatī attained the liberation door of universally manifesting all roots of goodness that bring coolness.
These roots of goodness are free from delusion and may thus be called 'cool,' just as Lake Anavatapta is forever free from the affliction of heat."
The River Deity Universal Joy-Producer (up to) the Gate of Liberation: Perpetual Freedom from Stinginess and Attachment.

The gates of giving are immeasurable; they cause others to be free from stinginess. Whether manifesting as duckweed, water lilies, lotus roots, or lotuses, they universally cause all beings to rejoice.
The River Spirit Sovereign of Vast Virtuous Banners attained the liberation door of becoming a field of merit that brings joy to all.
Because his practice of merit accords with reality, there is nothing that does not bring him delight. A deep lake or a vast marsh constitutes "vast virtue."
The Radiance Illuminating the Universal Sovereign River Deity (up to) the Gate of Joyful Liberation for Those Possessing the Poison of Hatred:

Through the power of skillful means and wisdom, all defilements are purified by compassion; those who harbor enmity and hatred are instead transformed into joy, like ten thousand acres of waves settling into clarity as light reflects across the world.
The River-God Ocean-Light Brilliance (up to): "The Liberation Gate of Constantly Receiving Perfect Joy.

This [gate] gathers all myriad virtues and leads them to Nirvana. Just as the hundred rivers all converge in the great ocean, because his wisdom is vast, he is named Ocean-Light Brilliance. △ Second, the verse praising the Buddha.
At that time, the River Spirit named Universally Emitting Swift Currents (up to: spoke these verses:
"The Tathāgata in the past, for the sake of sentient beings... (up to: "...this liberation of the spirit Sāgaraprabha."
△ Second, the Ten Deities of the Chief Harvesters. First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, from the "Deity of the Soft and Supreme Flavor Chief Harvester" (up to) "the gate of liberation that brings about the accomplishment of the Buddha-body."
The two kinds of dharma-flavors—merit and wisdom—sustain the formation of the Buddha-body.
At that time, the Flower-Pure-Light Crop-Master Spirit attained the liberation door of "Receiving Vast Great Joy and Bliss."
Joy and bliss arise from the removal of suffering.
This is the Dharma-gate of the Sovereign Deity of Crops, who brings strength, vigor, and courage to perfection; it is the liberation-door that purifies all realms.
Sentient beings are the objects to be purified.

[This is] the gate of liberation through the power of immeasurable great compassion and miraculous transformations, presided over by the deities who augment vital energy and govern the crops. (Up to...)
Because their compassion is profound, it is pervasive and vast.
[This is] the liberation door of the deity who presides over the roots, fruits, and crops of all beings, enabling them to sow seeds without loss or destruction.
When seeds are sown in the field of the Buddha, they will inevitably reach fruition without being ruined.
The field-protecting spirit Subhavyūhacūḍa attained the liberation door of universally inspiring pure faith in all sentient beings;
by spreading the wisdom that inspires faith in things, one obtains the flower of renown for the fruit.
The field-protecting spirit Vimalavibhūṣitā attained the liberation door of causing the ocean of merit and virtue to increase.
Because one views all things with eyes of loving-kindness, the accumulation of merit is immeasurable. Loving-kindness is serene, harmonious, and joyful. A verse says: "The Supreme Path.
The deity who presides over crops and mastery of fragrance attained the liberation door of being extensively shown all dharmas of practice.
Because he attained Buddhahood through practice, he proclaimed [the teaching] immediately upon his realization.
Those who behold it find joy; this is the liberation gate of the Lord of Crops (Sītavana-devaputra), wherein all evils are universally purified.
Laziness in cultivation gives rise to sorrow and affliction; by diligently restraining the sense faculties, all evils are purified.
This is the liberation door of the Crop-Master Deity Radiant and Free from Defilement, who causes the entire assembly to rejoice, be satisfied, and attain liberation.
He taught according to their faculties; they sought it and were thus filled with joy. △ Second, the verses in praise of the Buddha:
At that time, the field-protecting spirit named Mṛdumadhurarasādhya spoke in verse, saying:
From "The Tathāgata’s Unsurpassed Ocean of Merits" up to "this liberation door of the goddess Pure Light.
△ Eleven: The Primary Medicine Goddesses (2). First: The prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, the Auspicious Lord Medicine Deity [enters] the gate of liberation called "Diligently Gathering.
When things accord with one's inclinations, they are easily gathered; when they oppose one's intentions, they are difficult to harmonize. Therefore, he universally observes them all.
The medicinal goddess Candanavana-īśvarī [attains] the liberation door of extinguishing the afflictions of all sentient beings;
the second and third [goddesses] may be understood accordingly.
The medicinal goddess Viśrutaśabda-īśvarī [attains] the liberation door of increasing the boundless ocean of roots of goodness.
The Bodhisattva Śikṣānanda took the name "Real Guest"; the Great Being took the name "Buddha-Activity.
The Medicine-God King Pore-Light-Manifestation attained the liberation door of the sphere of all illnesses.

By the power of the roots of goodness of benevolence and compassion, they emit moon-like rays such as the "Moon-Love" light; the dual ailments of body and mind are extinguished the moment one brings them to mind.
This is the liberation door of the Medicine King Deity who Destroys Darkness and Purifies, which causes the eye of wisdom to become pure.

Deluded regarding principle and deluded regarding retribution, these two types of ignorance leave one in blinding darkness; they give rise to afflictions and create karma, causing one to undergo all manner of suffering.
The Buddha, with the golden scalpel of the True Dharma, opens their eye of wisdom, enabling them to clearly perceive the Three Truths; therefore, it is called "pure."
The medicinal deity Universal Roar-Emitting Lord (up to) the liberation door of causing all who see him to give rise to roots of goodness;
these two [deities] from seven to eight may be understood accordingly.
The medicinal deity Clearly Seeing the Ten Directions (up to) the liberation door of being able to use skillful means to cause the arising of faith and understanding.
The great compassion that is free from attachment and views generates virtue in all living beings; therefore, it is called a "Treasury.
[This is] the liberation gate of the Universal Radiance-Bringing Medicine Lord Spirit, which extinguishes the illnesses of all sentient beings.
Worldly physicians provide treatment, yet though the illness may be cured, it arises again; only the merit of eternally extinguishing birth is unsurpassed. Recalling the Buddha is the primary method;

both the cause of illness and the light [of the Buddha] are skillful means. This is because the Buddha possesses boundless marks (*lakṣaṇa*), each mark possesses boundless secondary signs (*anuvyañjana*), each secondary sign emits boundless light, and that light gathers in boundless multitudes.
As for the phrase "recalling according to [one's needs]," the Buddha’s virtues are uniform and equal; he accords with conditions and accords with inclinations.
If one takes refuge in a single Buddha, samādhi is easily accomplished; reverence becomes singular and the mind grows dense.
This is true for all others as well, let alone when the mind is concentrated on the path to awakening and one walks by intuition upon the Great Vehicle. II. Verses in Praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the Medicine Goddess Śrīmatī (up to) the Medicine Goddess Sarvavyavalokana addressed the assembly of all Medicine Goddesses in verse, saying:
"The wisdom of the Tathāgata is inconceivable... [this is] the liberation door of emitting this majestic light."
△ Second, the two [sections] on the twelve forest-deity chiefs. First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, the Forest-Deity Chief named Spreading Flowers Like Clouds attained the liberation door of the vast and boundless treasury of the ocean of wisdom.
The virtues of the Buddha are boundless and all rely upon the ocean of wisdom; because it contains virtue and radiates light, it is called a "Treasury.
The Forest-Ruling Spirit named Uplifting the Trunk and Spreading Light attained the liberation door of vast cultivation and universal purification.
Compassion for all sentient beings is what is called "vast. To be individually free from all obstacles is called "universal purity.
The Forest-Ruling Spirit named Producing the Sprouts of Various Pure Faiths attained the liberation door of the sprouting and radiating of [these] sprouts.
All supreme causes lead to the Buddha-way. When each mind is purified, various sprouts emerge.
This is the liberation door of the Forest-Ruling Spirit Auspicious Pure Leaf, called "The Array of All Pure Meritorious Qualities."
All merits adorn a single hair; each and every [hair] is likewise so. Therefore, the Buddha is a mass of virtues.

This is because the fruit of Buddhahood encompasses all causes, being perfectly accomplished rather than partially formed. Thus, one cause gives rise to all fruits, and one fruit subsumes all causes; they are entirely interfused and unimpeded.
The Forest-Ruling Spirit named Draped Flame Treasury (up to) the Gate of Liberation called Constantly Surveying the Dharma Realm:
Wisdom penetrates the myriad dharmas; this is called the Universal Gate (*samantamukha*). Because adventitious dust does not arise, it is called "pure.

Awakening is like the sun’s radiance, suddenly pervading the entire dharma realm. Its efficacy is like a Buddha-mirror; while the teaching of wisdom appears gradual, its clarity is primordial clarity (*mūlaprabhāsvara*), and this gradualness is for the sake of...
The simultaneous and gradual [attainment]. As the Forest-Ruling Spirit Master of Adorned Light (up to) the liberation door of spreading the clouds of Dharma.
Knowing the practices that lead everywhere, they are spread accordingly.
The forest deity Pleasing Thunder Sound [up to] attained the liberation door of manifesting pure sounds.

Because he realized that the nature of all sounds is identical to the Buddha’s voice, there was nothing unpleasant; he was able to cause the entire world to hear the Buddha’s voice, which alone can be called "pure."
From the Forest-Ruling Spirit Fragrant Light Pervading Everywhere (up to) the Gate of Liberation of the Sphere of Vast Practice:
In the past, her conduct was called "Pervading the Dharma Realm. This is the vast sphere; through her spiritual powers, she caused all beings to see it so that they might emulate and practice it.
The case of the one named *Hsī-mu* (Joyful Eye) below is precisely this matter.

From the gate of liberation of the Forest-Ruling Spirit Sublime Light Far-Shining, who benefits the world, [it is understood that] sentient beings are deceitful and do not cultivate virtue themselves;
how could they have the mind to advance others? Now, through merit and wisdom, they benefit others.
Thus, both self and others are benefited. The verse speaks of "deceit and perversity," which refers to flattery and sycophancy.
[The liberation door of] the Forest-Ruling Spirit of Flowers, Fruits, Light, and Flavor, up to the Liberation Door of the Treasury of Adorned Merits.

When one reverently recollects, the Buddha appears; when the Buddha appears, his treasury of majestic virtues is manifested. For those whose obstructions are heavy, they do not recollect and do not see him;
yet is the Buddha not eternal? Therefore, for those who should see him, he is seen at all times. △ Second, the verse in praise of the Buddha.
At that time, the forest-dwelling spirit named Flower-Spreading-Cloud spoke in verse:
"In the past, the Buddha cultivated and accumulated the practices for enlightenment... [this flavor-light spirit has observed it]."
△ Thirteenth: The Primary Mountain Deity (2). First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.
Furthermore, the primary mountain deity Jewel Peak Blooming Flowers attained the liberation door of the light of entry into the great tranquil concentration.
Because it is quiescent yet ever-illuminating, its light leaves nothing unmanifested.
[This is] the liberation door of the Mountain Spirit Wondrous Topknot of Flower Forests (up to), which brings to maturity an inconceivable number of sentient beings.
The maturation of capacities through the light of marks is entirely due to the power of the roots of goodness of benevolence and compassion, as explained at length in the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.
[This is the liberation door of] the mountain spirit High Banner Illumining Everywhere, who delights in purifying the sense faculties with her heart.

Cultivating the causes to adorn the faculties is fundamentally for the sake of harmonizing with all things; thus, one rejoices upon beholding lotus-like eyes and feels gladness of heart upon seeing a moon-like face.
Or, when one perceives that all the faculties are entirely pervasive throughout the Dharma-realm, one’s joy and benefit become even deeper.
From the mountain spirit Virajamaulī to the liberation door of untiring diligence,
they remain unstained like space, and thus remain indefatigable throughout long eons.
The Mountain Spirit Sovereign Illuminating the Ten Directions attained the liberation door of universally awakening through boundless merit-light;
for due to delusion one sleeps long, and only through the power of merit and wisdom can one awaken.
The mountain deity Great Power Radiance Lord [up to] the liberation door of manifesting the merits of all Tathāgatas—
these three preceding [sections] may be understood.
The mountain deity Universal Eye Manifest Vision Lord [up to] the liberation door of increasing roots of goodness within dreams.
Whether asleep or awake, causing all to hear the Dharma and progress therein is the work of a Buddha. As stated in the *Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra*:
"In the past, there was a Buddha who, whenever he wished to preach the Dharma, caused the great assembly to sleep;

he then preached the Dharma within their dreams, causing them to increase their roots of goodness and awaken to the fruits of the Path. The *Nirvāṇa-sūtra* also says: "That person, in a dream, saw the image of a rākṣasa," and so forth.
It also signifies that all phenomena are a dream. In the night of the great dream, there must be the illumination of great awakening.
The Mountain Deity, Lord of the Vajra-Firm Eye, attained the liberation door of manifesting the ocean of boundless great meanings.
The Dharma-gate that accords with the nature of reality possesses boundless great meaning; that a single sound can expound it is its manifestation.
△ Second, the verse praise of the Buddha:
At that time, the Earth-Ruling Mountain Deity named Flower-Enveloping spoke these verses:
Having cultivated supreme practices without limit, one enters this Vajra-Eye expedient. △ Fourteen:
The Earth-Ruling Spirit (Dharanīndrā). Part Two: First, the prose section on attaining the Dharma.

Furthermore, from the Earth-Ruling Spirit Samantaguṇaviśuddhikusuma (Samantaguṇaviśuddhikusumādhipati) up to [the description of] the gate of universally observing the liberation of all sentient beings:
in every thought-moment, without interruption, she observes all equally and universally, cultivating loving-kindness and protecting the Dharma; therefore, she attains a vajra-body.
Vajra is precisely the reality of internal illumination.
The earth goddess Firmly Adorned with Merit attained the liberation door of universally manifesting the power of the merit of all sentient beings;
by the power of the merit of a single hair, she suddenly manifests the merit of all beings.
The Earth-Ruling Spirit named Wondrous Flower Adorned Tree entered the liberation door of producing all adornments of Buddha-fields;
she realized non-arising and was unimpeded in adorning the fields.
The Earth-Ruling Spirit Universal Dispenser of Myriad Jewels [attains] the liberation door of causing sentient beings to eliminate hindrances and defilements;
the Earth-Ruling Spirit Pure Eye Contemplating Time [attains] the liberation door of constantly sporting in joy for the sake of others alone.
Manifesting in accordance with the capacities of beings is called "playful manifestation.
[This concludes the section on] the Earth-Ruling Goddess Golden Wondrous Eye’s liberation door of taming sentient beings through a pure body.
Manifesting a body purified of afflictions, she then tames the afflictions of sentient beings.
[This is] the liberation door of the earth-ruling goddess Fragrant-Hair-Radiance, which possesses the great majestic power of the ocean of all Buddhas' merits.

Internally possessing an ocean of virtues, he manifests a body of majestic power; like the earth containing the moisture of the ocean, he brings forth the hundred grains, for all the sprouts and crops of the hundred grains are due to the fragrant vapors of the earth.
The Earth-Ruling Spirit named Tranquil Sound Pleasing to the Mind attained the liberation door of universally upholding the ocean of all vocal sounds.
A single word of her prose encompasses everything without exception; a single word of her verse is universally pervasive and infinite.
The earth-ruling spirit Wondrous Flower Swirling Topknot attained the liberation door of the stainless nature that fills buddha-fields;
its nature is to cause all beings to leave behind defilement through the universal pervasion of clouds of radiance.
From the Earth Goddess Vajra-Universal-Sustainer (up to) the liberation gate of the universal manifestation sustained by the wheel of Dharma.
The Dharma can sustain mental activities just as a vajra-wheel sustains the Buddha, who remains unmoving while manifesting in the world, like Mount Sumeru emerging from the ocean.
△ Second, the praise of the Buddha in verse.
At that time, the earth goddess Samantataḥpuṇyaprasavāśuddhaharṣā (up to) spoke these verses.
Within these verses that follow, there are also two lines that conclude by attributing the Dharma to a person; this can be understood through reflection.
"In every thought-moment of the Tathāgata’s past... (up to)... he universally upholds and beholds them, giving rise to joy.
△ Fifteenth, the City-Ruling Goddesses, Part Two. First, the prose section contains ten dharmas. Some say that the ninth and tenth are omitted [in the prose], while they are complete in the verse.
Furthermore, the city-ruling spirit Jewel-Peak Radiance attained the liberation door of benefiting sentient beings through skillful means;
she brings them to maturity and benefits them through equalizing skillful means.
The goddess Sovereign of the Palace of Sublime Adornment attained the gate of teaching, maturing, and liberating sentient beings by knowing their characteristics;
she dispenses medicine according to the ailment, enabling them to take it and practice.
The City-Ruling Goddess Pūrṇaprasannarati-ratna (up to) the liberation gate through which all sentient beings receive various merits and virtues.
When the Dharma is protected and the teachings endure, then beings receive merit and virtue; thus, the teaching, the principle, the practice, and the fruit are all protected.
The city-ruling spirit Free from Sorrow and Pure attained the liberation door of the treasury of great compassion that rescues all from fear.
The city-ruling spirit Flower Lamp Flame Eye attained the liberation door of the vast, all-illuminating, great wisdom.

The City-Ruling Spirit Attaining Universal Expedient Means Manifestation realized the great wisdom of the Buddha and attained the liberation door of manifesting expedient bodies. The Flame Banner Radiance City-Ruling Spirit attained the liberation door of the manifestation of universal expedient means.
She manifested her body through these expedient means.
The City-Ruling Spirit Abundant Merit and Majestic Radiance [attains] the liberation door of awakening all ignorant and dark sentient beings.

Because they are deluded regarding the principles of ultimate and conventional truth, they are called "ignorant and dark. When a Buddha appears and reveals them, he causes them to awaken and enter [the truth].
